author: Binay Verma
status: Exploratory. Registered and committed before any sunday_day forecast exists, but on India cases whose other arms were already inspected. Not a confirmation and not a preregistration in the external sense.
question: Does Ziel (2018) replacing encoding (festival day treated as Sunday, no additive indicator) differ from the additive pooled and typed day indicators for the local models on the same cases?
source_method: Ziel, F. (2018). Modeling public holidays in load forecasting: a German case study. Journal of Modern Power Systems and Clean Energy 6(2), 191-207. Replacing holiday-as-Sunday variant, adapted to daily festival anchors.
new_arm_definition: 13 calendar channels; on every document-aligned anchor date of any of the five families (identical dates to pooled_day5 event_day) dow_0..dow_5 = 0 and dow_6 = 1; plus five zero channels (18 channels, equal to the other event arms). Applied to training and query dates alike.
local_design: Ridge/LightGBM: the registered rich-history design; its 13 calendar columns are replaced in place by the arm frame at the target date, then the arm extra channels are appended. Reference arms therefore reproduce the parent matrix exactly. SARIMAX(1,0,0)(1,0,0,7): the whole 18- or 13-channel arm frame is the exogenous input.
selection: No search. Reuse the stored past-selected parameters (strong_refit_v1, stable_tree_refit_v2) unchanged; capacity2 override min_child_samples=2 as before. Monthly refits as in the parent engine.
cases: event_window: the 528 composed document-aligned window cases (176 state-dates x leads 1, 7, 14). ordinary: the 216 composed ordinary cases. Taken from the composed analysis files listed in input_hashes.
reproduction_check: Reference-arm predictions must match the stored document_aligned predictions for the same model, arm and case within atol 1e-7 GWh, rtol 1e-9. Any mismatch is reported as a failure and the new arm is not interpreted.
metrics: Row MASE = |prediction - actual| / fixed pre-year 730-day weekly scale. Balanced event MASE = mean over families of mean over years of mean over states of mean row MASE (the v6 hierarchy). Ordinary cohort: mean over years of mean over states.
reporting: Leads 1, 7 and 14 for every model. For each contrast: balanced value, family-year cluster signs, leave-one-family-out range and sign flips, and 2024 versus 2025 values. Ordinary-cohort cost of each arm versus calendar. No p-values, no bootstrap, no winner selection; negative and null results are reported.
interpretation: A contrast is described as consistent only if its sign holds in both years and in every leave-one-family-out subset; otherwise it is described as unstable. Values with absolute size below 0.005 MASE are called negligible.
